description: Thevenin Simulation Engine - SPICE circuit simulator library in Rust, rewriting ngspice. 108 harness tests total (107 .cir files with .out references; 6 .cir files lack .out and are skipped; 1 has 'To be done' reference and should be permanently ignored). Currently 29 genuinely verified, 41 vacuously passing (US-070), 38 ignored in ignore.toml. True progress: 29/107 genuine passes.

passLog.summary: Ported regression tests for models, subcircuit processing, temperature, and misc: implemented .if/.elseif/.else/.endif preprocessor, model-referenced resistors, model name scoping in subcircuits, .temp directive parsing, ac= source parsing. Added 15 tests across regression_misc.rs, regression_model.rs, and regression_subckt.rs. Several tests deferred due to missing features (temper keyword, .control language, tc1 on B-sources, model binning).

Split US-039 (was too large: harness + all 113 passing). Added US-052 (BSIM1), US-053 (BSIM2), US-054 (remaining regression tests), US-055 (general/filter/pz/sens tests), US-056 (XSPICE, lowest priority). Marked US-044 obsolete (superseded by US-049). Reordered priorities: implementation/testing (39-43) before architecture/API (46-48) before polish/publish (56-60). Sequenced US-043 (docs) after US-049 (API design).

Built test harness matching ngspice check.sh: per-file test functions for all 113 .cir files via macro, batch-mode output formatter, check.sh FILTER port, 30s per-test timeout, nextest integration. 19/107 tests passing, 45 tests #[ignore]d (BSIM1/BSIM2/XSPICE/scripting). All pre-existing 465 tests still pass.

Fixed DC sweep variable column naming (v-sweep/i-sweep instead of source name). Added numeric tolerance comparison (1e-4 relative) to compare_filtered() for handling FP differences between implementations. Un-ignored 2 harness tests (hfet/id_vgs, mesa/mesa14). Updated remaining ignore reasons to reflect actual root causes. 21/107 harness tests now passing.

Added interpolation-aware fallback to compare_filtered() for handling different adaptive timestep sequences. When line counts differ, data sections are compared by linearly interpolating actual values at expected time points. Un-ignored resistance/res_simple (now passes). Updated 11 harness ignore reasons to reflect actual root causes (device info output, singular matrices, numerical accuracy). 22/107 harness tests now passing.

Fixed PZ complex pair formatting (real,imag), merged pole/zero tables (2 cols/page), sensitivity pagination (4 cols/page), TF plot naming (sequential tf1/tf2), format_sci edge case, removed Index vector from sens. Un-ignored 4 PZ tests (simplepz, filt_rc, pzt, filt_multistage). 26/108 harness tests now passing.
Added US-066 (.control scripting batch subset, priority 47) to unblock ~39 regression tests. Added US-067 (BJT sensitivity parameter completeness, priority 48) to fix sensitivity/diffpair.
Partial progress on US-059 (BSIM3SOI convergence). Fixed NCH/NPEAK alias sync and vbi formula in all 3 models.
Fixed BSIM3SOI-FD floating body architecture. All 4 active FD tests pass.
Fixed BSIM3SOI-DD Abulk formula, XJ default, Xcsat/Abeff. DD t3 error improved from ~65% to ~10%.
Deprioritized US-059 (43->90) after 3 iterations without resolving PD convergence.
PRD reevaluation. Nominally 70/108 passing but discovered 41 vacuous passes. Updated all 'cargo test' to 'cargo nextest run'.
Deep investigation confirmed vacuous pass problem. True pass count 29/108. Reverted US-066 and US-056. Added US-070.

Major PRD restructure. Merges: US-052+US-063 (BSIM1 parser+model), US-053+US-064 (BSIM2 parser+model), US-050+US-051 (type safety+unwraps into US-075 code quality), US-041+US-042+US-047+US-048 (publish checklist into US-076). Splits: US-060 into US-071 (VBIC self-heating) and US-072 (transmission line accuracy). US-068 trimmed to 3 focused tests, added US-073 (fourbitadder perf), removed diffpair (no reference). Removed US-062 (.plot parser, unnecessary). Added US-074 (@device[param] query). Archived US-059 (BSIM3SOI, p90). Reprioritized: US-070 (p1) > US-066 (p2) > US-071 (p3) > US-072 (p4) > US-068 (p5).

userStories.title: Fix vacuous test passes in harness comparison
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the harness to honestly report test results by detecting and handling tests where both expected and actual output filter to zero parseable data rows.
acceptanceCriteria: Tests whose .cir files have ALL analyses inside .control blocks (and no Item::Analysis outside) are moved to ignore.toml with reason 'requires .control scripting (US-066)'
Tests with non-trivial expected .out but zero parseable data on both sides are flagged (not silently Ok)
The 3 XSPICE tests are moved to ignore.toml with reason 'requires XSPICE + .control (US-066, US-056)'
general/rca3040, mesa/mesa13, mesa/mesa21 are explicitly annotated as 'correctly empty (no .print directive)'
general/diffpair permanently ignored with reason 'reference output says To be done'
After fix, cargo nextest run shows only genuinely-verified passes (no false positives)
userStories.notes: CRITICAL — must be done first so all subsequent progress is trustworthy. 41 of 70 nominally-passing tests are vacuously passing because compare_with_interpolation returns Ok when both exp_data and act_data are empty (output.rs:2318). Quick fix: detect .control-only tests at compile time in the proc macro (or at runtime in run_embedded_test) and auto-ignore them. This will drop the nominal pass count from 70 to ~29 but those 29 are real.

userStories.title: .control scripting language (batch subset)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the .control/.endc scripting block to be handled in batch mode so that the ~38 regression tests that use .control can run and be genuinely verified.
acceptanceCriteria: 'run' inside .control triggers all analyses declared in the netlist (equivalent to batch mode)
'print <var>' inside .control produces the same output as .print outside (batch-mode table format)
'echo <text>' outputs the text string to stdout
Unsupported .control commands (define, if/else/end, quit) are silently skipped
Un-ignores: all 38 .control-dependent tests from US-070 and they genuinely pass
userStories.notes: The parser currently silently skips .control blocks (parse.rs:1465-1474, produces Item::Raw('')). Needs to either: (A) extract commands into structured items during parsing, or (B) process .control blocks as a post-parse step in the harness/simulator. Option B is simpler — scan for .control block text, parse the subset of commands, convert 'run' to 'run all analyses', 'print' to Item::Print, etc. Most .control tests use only run+print+echo+let. Some use 'define' for custom functions and if/else for validation — those can be deferred.

userStories.title: Fix VBIC self-heating FP accuracy
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the VBIC model's self-heating computation to match ngspice's FP evaluation order so the 5 VBIC tests pass.
userStories.notes: Split from old US-060. All 5 failures share one root cause: self-heating FP evaluation order. FG/FO/temp have ~0.2% DC errors that grow linearly with Vrth — suggests an accumulated FP difference in the thermal subcircuit computation. CEamp has 0.2% AC gain error from the same root. diffamp is NR non-convergence in a complex self-heating circuit. The errors are very close to the 0.2% tolerance — fixing the evaluation order could push all 4 below threshold. vbic/noise_scale already passes.

userStories.title: Fix transmission line test accuracy
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the 4 remaining transmission line harness tests to pass by improving CMOS switching accuracy in the driver circuits.
userStories.notes: Split from old US-060. ltra1_1 already passes. The remaining failures are NOT transmission line model bugs — they're caused by CMOS driver switching accuracy. CPL tests (cpl3_4, cpl_ibm2) have the largest errors (~13-61%) from constant junction cap approximation in the MOSFET models driving the lines. TXL tests (~4.6%) are from TXL-specific model timing. ltra2_2 (~5.8%) accumulates errors through cascaded stages. Root cause investigation should focus on junction capacitance modeling in the MOSFET driver transistors.

userStories.title: Fix general circuit model accuracy (mosamp, rtlinv, schmitt, hfet/inverter)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the remaining general circuit harness tests to pass by fixing model accuracy and convergence issues.
acceptanceCriteria: general/mosamp passes (Level 2 MOSFET velocity saturation/mobility degradation)
general/rtlinv passes (BJT transient timing within tolerance)
general/schmitt passes (BJT switching accuracy within tolerance)
hfet/inverter DC OP converges to correct solution (V(3)=-0.275V, not 1.96V)
userStories.notes:
Trimmed from old US-068 (removed fourbitadder → US-073, removed diffpair → permanently ignored). Four distinct issues:
- mosamp: ~35% error. Level 2 MOSFET missing velocity saturation and mobility degradation. Requires model enhancement.
- rtlinv: ~4.1% transient error at t=9ns. Close to tolerance. BJT dynamic caps improved it from 5.96% to 4.1% — may need further cap accuracy work.
- schmitt: ~31% error at t=293ns. Output oscillation during switching. BJT caps are dynamic but timing errors dominate.
- hfet/inverter: wrong stable point. Bistable DCFL inverter converges to Vdd instead of low output. Source stepping also fails. May need different initial guess or continuation method.

userStories.title: Performance: fourbitadder timeout
userStories.description: As a developer, I need general/fourbitadder and transient/fourbitadder to complete within the 30s timeout by optimizing simulation performance.
acceptanceCriteria: No regression in accuracy for other tests
userStories.notes: Split from old US-068. Pure performance issue — the fourbitadder circuits time out (>30s). These are large transient simulations with many MOSFET devices. Likely needs sparse matrix optimization, timestep control improvements, or convergence speedups. Low priority since it's only 2 tests and the issue is speed, not correctness.

userStories.title: Sensitivity analysis: LU precision for diffpair
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the sensitivity analysis to preserve bit-exact LU factorization from the NR solver so that sensitivity/diffpair passes.
acceptanceCriteria: Sensitivity computation reuses the sparse LU factorization from the converged NR solution
userStories.notes: Updated title/description to reflect actual root cause (was 'BJT parameter completeness'). The failure is now: 'q3/q4:is sensitivity requires bit-exact LU reuse from NR solver (dense LU refactoring loses CMRR precision)'. The sensitivity perturbation computation loses precision when it re-factors the Jacobian using dense LU instead of reusing the sparse factorization from the NR solve.

userStories.title: Runtime parameter expressions and TEMPER keyword
userStories.description: As a developer, I need runtime parameter expressions (r={1k + v(9)}) and the TEMPER keyword so the last 2 misc regression tests pass.
acceptanceCriteria: regression/misc/asrc-tc-2.cir passes (parameter expressions like r={1k + v(9)})
userStories.notes: Two small features. asrc-tc-2 needs voltage-dependent parameter expressions (r={1k + v(9)}) which are evaluated at each NR iteration — this is different from static .param expressions. temper-3 needs the TEMPER keyword which expands to the current simulation temperature. Both also require .control scripting (US-066) since the test validation uses .control blocks.

userStories.title: @device[param] query and .print expression support
userStories.description: As a developer, I need .print to support @device[param] queries (e.g. @m1[Vbs]) and inline expressions (e.g. V(g)/10) so that BSIM3SOI RampVg2 tests can produce output.
acceptanceCriteria: @m1[param] syntax in .print resolves to the named device's internal parameter value
V(node)/constant and similar simple expressions in .print are evaluated
BSIM3SOI-DD/FD/PD RampVg2 tests produce non-empty output (correctness depends on US-059)
userStories.notes: NEW. Three BSIM3SOI RampVg2 tests are ignored with 'empty output: @m1[Vbs] device parameter query and V(g)/10 expression not supported in .print'. This is independent of the BSIM3SOI convergence issue (US-059) — even if the model converged, these tests would produce empty output. Implementing device parameter queries requires: (1) parser support for @name[param] in .print variable lists, (2) runtime resolution against device instance state after simulation, (3) expression evaluation in .print variables.

userStories.title: XSPICE digital models (d_ram, d_source, d_state)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need XSPICE code model execution for the 3 digital test circuits. Depends on .control scripting (US-066) since all 3 tests use .control for their tran analysis.
acceptanceCriteria: XSPICE A-element instances are dispatched to registered code models during simulation
d_source reads stimulus file and produces digital events
d_ram implements addressed read/write with digital I/O
d_state implements state machine from description file
All 3 xspice/digital harness tests genuinely pass (non-vacuous)
userStories.notes: Depends on US-066 (.control) since all 3 .cir files use .control for tran/eprint. The thevenin-xspice crate has a code model framework (registry, parameter types, port handling, stamping API) but no built-in digital models. Also needs harness support for XSPICE digital event output format (non-integer-indexed rows with digital state tokens like 0s/1s/Us).

userStories.title: [ARCHIVED] BSIM3SOI convergence and model accuracy
userStories.description: Fix BSIM3SOI DD/FD/PD convergence failures and model accuracy. ARCHIVED at priority 90 — 3 iterations spent without resolving PD convergence. Root cause is likely a bug in companion model or MNA stamp Jacobian for the body node.
userStories.notes: ARCHIVED. 15 tests: DD (5), FD (5), PD (5). Convergence issues (singular matrix) in inv2 tests for all 3. Model value bugs in t3/t4/t5. RampVg2 blocked by US-074 (@device[param] query). Extensive investigation documented in iterations 27-30. Fixed: NCH/NPEAK sync, vbi formula, FD floating body architecture, DD Abulk/XJ/Xcsat. Remaining: PD body node oscillation — likely wrong sign/missing current/incorrect Jacobian in companion model.

userStories.title: Code quality: type safety and error handling
userStories.description: As a library consumer, I need thevenin to encode invariants in the type system and never panic, so the API is safe and all errors are recoverable.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit and replace raw primitives with newtypes where constraints exist (NonNegative, NodeIndex, Frequency)
Replace stringly-typed fields with enums where a fixed set of variants exists
Eliminate boolean flag pairs that represent mutually exclusive states — use enums
All fallible operations return Result with meaningful error variants
Test code and examples are exempt from unwrap/panic restrictions
userStories.notes: Merged US-050 (make incorrect states unrepresentable) + US-051 (eliminate unwraps). Both are code quality passes through the same files — doing them together avoids touching every file twice. Focus on high-impact areas first: public API types, device model configuration, analysis parameters. The codebase was ported from C which uses assert/abort patterns.

acceptanceCriteria: All publishable crates (thevenin, thevenin-types, thevenin-xspice, thevenin-cirq) have: license, repository, homepage, keywords, categories, readme fields in Cargo.toml
cargo publish --dry-run succeeds for all publishable crates
BSD-3-Clause LICENSE file at repository root
Root README.md with project description, feature overview, quick-start, supported analyses/models, MSRV, license badge
CHANGELOG.md at root (Keep a Changelog format) with initial entry
RELEASING.md documenting publish process and crate ordering (thevenin-types -> thevenin-xspice -> thevenin -> thevenin-cirq)
ngspice-upstream/ and scripts/ excluded from published crates

userStories.notes: Merged US-041 (Cargo.toml metadata) + US-042 (LICENSE/README) + US-047 (CHANGELOG/release) + US-048 (crate size audit). These are all checklist items for the same milestone (first publish) and don't require deep engineering. Current state: 6 workspace crates, versions inconsistent (0.2.0 vs 0.1.x), no LICENSE/README/CHANGELOG, CLI is 'Hello world', ngspice-upstream ~100MB must be excluded.
